summary: You can feed adult donkeys, horses, llamas or mules with maximum Temper value, and hand animation is not played
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a Creative world.
2. Run `/summon horse ~ ~ ~ {Temper:100}`.
3. Select any food item.
4. Use the food item on the summoned adult horse.
5. Observe that the food is consumed without the hand animation, eating sounds, or other feeding animations being played.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.17.1, 21w37a, 21w38a, 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1, 1.18 Pre-release 2, 1.18 Pre-release 4, 1.18 Pre-release 5, 1.18 Pre-release 6, 1.18 Pre-release 8, 1.18 Release Candidate 3, 1.18, 1.18.1 Release Candidate 2, 1.18.1, 22w03a, 22w06a, 1.18.2 Pre-release 1, 22w11a, 22w17a, 22w18a, 1.19 Pre-release 1, 1.19, 1.19.1 Pre-release 5, 1.19.2, 22w42a, 22w46a, 23w06a, 1.19.4, 23w18a, 1.20 Release Candidate 1, 1.20, 1.20.1, 1.20.2 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
## Actual behavior

When an adult, untamed donkey, horse, llama, or mule has its `Temper` value at the maximum (`100` in the reproduction example), interacting with it while holding valid food consumes the food despite the animal already having maximum Temper.

The interaction does not play the usual player hand-swing animation or the animal’s eating sound/animation. This is not a client–server desynchronization: the food is actually consumed by the animal. The issue occurs with all applicable food items, although a golden carrot may very rarely play the animation and sound once, typically on the first interaction.
Expected Behavior: When an adult donkey, horse, llama, or mule has reached its maximum Temper value, attempting to feed it should play the normal hand animation and interaction sounds, but the animal should not consume the food or otherwise change. This behavior should be consistent for all applicable food items and should occur reliably, without occasionally consuming food or playing the effects only once.
